FORMAL NOTICE FOR REFUND OF SECURITY DEPOSIT

Date: 08 November 2026

To,
Mrs. Preeti Kaur
(Landlord / Property Owner)
Property: House No. 1124, Sector 35-C, Chandigarh 160035

From,
Aman Deep Singh
(Former Tenant)
Contact: [Tenant Phone / Email]

Subject: Formal Demand for Immediate Refund of Outstanding Security Deposit of ₹10,000

Dear Mrs. Preeti Kaur,

I am issuing this formal demand notice regarding the residential premises situated at:
House No. 1124, Sector 35-C, Chandigarh 160035.

1. TENANCY PARTICULARS:
I was residing as a tenant at the above-mentioned premises and peacefully handed over vacant possession upon moving out on 28 October 2025. The tenancy was established under an oral tenancy agreement with mutual terms.

2. SECURITY DEPOSIT ACCOUNTING:
The payment of the security deposit of ₹25,000 was made upon commencement and is evidenced by verified transaction records / receipts.
To date, you have returned ₹15,000, leaving an unpaid deposit balance of ₹10,000.

3. UNJUSTIFIED WITHHOLDING / DEDUCTIONS:
You have purportedly withheld/deducted ₹10,000 citing 'deep cleaning and AC servicing'. Please take note that under applicable law, specifically Section 11 of the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Security deposit limit and mandatory refund timeline); Section 15 of the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Division of maintenance responsibilities and routine wear and tear), a security deposit is held in trust solely to secure against tenant breach or damage beyond reasonable wear and tear. Arbitrary deductions without providing itemized repair bills, GST invoices, and prior joint inspection records are legally impermissible and constitute unjust retention of funds.

4. LEGAL POSITION:
Under applicable Indian statutes, specifically Section 11 of the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Security deposit limit and mandatory refund timeline); Section 15 of the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (Division of maintenance responsibilities and routine wear and tear), a landlord is legally required to return the security deposit promptly upon vacant handover, subject only to demonstrable, itemized actual loss beyond reasonable wear and tear. Unilateral deductions without documentary proof and verified invoices amount to breach of trust and unlawful retention of tenant funds.

5. FORMAL DEMAND:
You are hereby called upon to refund the outstanding sum of ₹10,000 within 15 (fifteen) days from the receipt of this notice, payable to the following bank account / UPI ID:
Payment Details: [Your Bank Name, Account Number, IFSC Code or UPI ID]

In the event of failure to refund the said sum within 15 days, I shall be constrained to initiate formal legal remedies before the competent Rent Authority, Civil Court, Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, or approach the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / Lok Adalat for recovery, holding you liable for all legal expenses, damages, and statutory interest.

Sincerely,

Aman Deep Singh
(Former Tenant)

product_innovation_pushback_simulator.title: Tactic 2: Notice Period Forfeiture ("You didn't give 2 months notice")
product_innovation_pushback_simulator.landlord_message: "You vacated suddenly without giving a full 2-month advance written notice. Your deposit is therefore forfeited as rent in lieu of notice."
product_innovation_pushback_simulator.legal_position: Under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the statutory notice period for residential tenancies is 15 days. Moreover, under Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, automatic forfeiture of a security deposit constitutes an impermissible penalty. A landlord is legally required to mitigate losses by re-letting and can only claim actual proven vacancy loss.

# PRE-LITIGATION CASE DOSSIER & COMPLAINT PETITION

**BEFORE THE HON'BLE DISTRICT CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION /**  
**BEFORE THE SECRETARY, DISTRICT LEGAL SERVICES AUTHORITY (DLSA)**  
**AT CHANDIGARH, CHANDIGARH**

---

### IN THE MATTER OF:
**TENANT / COMPLAINANT**  
*(Details as per Lease Agreement)*  
`... COMPLAINANT`

**VERSUS**

**LANDLORD / OPPOSITE PARTY**  
*(Property Owner / Lessor)*  
`... OPPOSITE PARTY`

---

## 1. SYNOPSIS & LIST OF DATES AND EVENTS

| Date | Event / Fact | Statutory Nexus |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tenancy Inception** | Complainant entered into residential tenancy in Chandigarh, Chandigarh and transferred ₹25,000 as refundable security deposit. | Section 10, Indian Contract Act, 1872 & Section 61, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 |
| **28 October 2025** | Complainant lawfully vacated premises and peacefully surrendered keys following joint handover. | Section 108(q), Transfer of Property Act, 1882 |
| **+30 Days Post-Exit** | Statutory 30-day refund window elapsed. Opposite Party failed to return full deposit or tender itemized GST invoices. | Section 11, Model Tenancy Act, 2021 |
| **Dispute Date** | Opposite Party unilaterally withheld ₹10,000 under the pretext of 'deep cleaning and AC servicing', without supplying third-party contractor tax invoices. | Section 73 & 74, Indian Contract Act, 1872 |
| **Notice Served** | Complainant served formal 15-day statutory demand notice requesting refund or production of genuine GST bills. | Consumer Protection Act, 2019 §2(11) |
| **Present Date** | Opposite Party failed to comply. Present complaint/conciliation petition instituted for recovery of ₹10,400. | Section 21, Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 |

---

## 2. STATUTORY GROUNDS & STATEMENT OF CLAIM

1. **Unilateral Breach of Contract (Section 73, Indian Contract Act, 1872):**  
   The security deposit was delivered in trust solely to guarantee tenancy covenants. A landlord cannot unilaterally deduct funds for 'deep cleaning and AC servicing' without proving actual, non-remote financial injury through certified receipts.

2. **Violation of Statutory Notice and Billing Mandate (Section 11, Model Tenancy Act, 2021):**  
   Section 11 strictly mandates that any deduction must be substantiated with itemized accounts and actual expenditure bills. In the absence of third-party contractor GST invoices, withholding constitutes an arbitrary penalty barred under Section 74 of the ICA.

3. **Admissibility of Electronic Records (Section 61, Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023):**  
   The Complainant substantiates all financial transactions (deposit transfer of ₹25,000 and partial return of ₹15,000) through bank account statements and UPI transaction logs, forming admissible primary electronic evidence.

4. **Deficiency of Service (Section 2(11), Consumer Protection Act, 2019):**  
   The arbitrary retention of tenancy deposits by a landlord constitutes an unfair practice and deficiency in service, entitling the consumer to restitution and compensation.

---

## 3. PRAYER & RELIEF SOUGHT

WHEREFORE, the Complainant respectfully prays that this Hon'ble Authority / Commission may be pleased to:

* **A. Direct the Opposite Party** to immediately refund the unlawfully withheld principal sum of **₹10,000** to the Complainant.
* **B. Award Statutory Interest** of **₹400** (calculated @ 8% p.a. from expiry of 30 days post move-out till actual realization) under the Interest Act, 1978.
* **C. Grant Reasonable Litigation Costs & Nominal Compensation** of ₹5,000/- for mental harassment and unjust deprivation of hard-earned funds.
* **D. Pass any other order(s)** deemed just and equitable in the interest of justice.

---

| **Annexure C-5** | Proof of Service (India Post Registered AD Tracking / WhatsApp Delivery). | Establishes delivery and opposite party's default. |
